briefdescription.para: The operation is expected to be selectable directly by the target, and no transformation is necessary.
The operation should be synthesized from multiple instructions acting on a narrower scalar base-type.

detaileddescription.para: For example a 64-bit add might be implemented in terms of 32-bit add-with-carry.

briefdescription.para: The operation should be implemented in terms of a wider scalar base-type.

detaileddescription.para: For example a <2 x s8> add could be implemented as a <2 x s32> add (ignoring the high bits).

briefdescription.para: The (vector) operation should be implemented by splitting it into sub-vectors where the operation is legal.

detaileddescription.para: For example a <8 x s64> add might be implemented as 4 separate <2 x s64> adds. There can be a leftover if there are not enough elements for last sub-vector e.g. <7 x s64> add will be implemented as 3 separate <2 x s64> adds and one s64 add. Leftover types can be avoided by doing MoreElements first.

briefdescription.para: The (vector) operation should be implemented by widening the input vector and ignoring the lanes added by doing so.

detaileddescription.para: For example <2 x i8> is rarely legal, but you might perform an <8 x i8> and then only look at the first two results.

briefdescription.para: Perform the operation on a different, but equivalently sized type.
The operation itself must be expressed in terms of simpler actions on this target.

detaileddescription.para: E.g. a SREM replaced by an SDIV and subtraction.

briefdescription.para: The operation should be implemented as a call to some kind of runtime support library.

detaileddescription.para: For example this usually happens on machines that don't support floating-point operations natively.

briefdescription.para: The target wants to do something special with this combination of operand and type.

detaileddescription.para: A callback will be issued when it is needed.

briefdescription.para: This operation is completely unsupported on the target.
Sentinel value for when no action was found in the specified table.
Fall back onto the old rules.
